style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The last of the church's seven penitential psalms, and the one Paul reached for when he wrote that by works of the law no flesh will be justified -- verse 2 is his text (Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16). David is hunted, crushed to the ground, made to sit in darkness like the long dead, his spirit failing inside him -- and before he asks for a single thing against his enemies, he settles the one thing that matters between himself and God: do not enter into judgment with Your servant, for in Your sight no one living is righteous. Everything else in the psalm rests on that plea being granted. What follows is the anatomy of a faith that fights for its footing: he remembers the days of old and muses on God's works; he spreads out his hands like a parched land opening for rain; he asks to hear covenant love in the morning, to be shown the way to walk, to be taught to do God's will by God's good Spirit, to be led on level ground. The requests are all downstream of one relationship, stated three times as the psalm's warrant: I am Your servant. A guilty man with no defense, asking his Master for mercy, guidance, and life -- and expecting all three.

1.text: A psalm of David. Hear my prayer, O LORD; give ear to my pleadings for grace; in Your faithfulness answer me, and in Your righteousness.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Hear [shama] my prayer [tephillah], O LORD [YHWH], give ear [azan] to my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace]: in Your faithfulness [emunah] answer [anah] me, and in Your righteousness [tsedaqah].
1.notes: The two attributes David asks to be answered BY: emunah and tsedaqah (H530, H6666), faithfulness and righteousness -- a bold pairing for a penitent, until verse 2 shows he means God's righteousness in keeping covenant, not in weighing David (cf. 1 John 1:9, where the same two words secure forgiveness).

2.text: And do not enter into judgment with Your servant, for in Your sight no one living can be declared righteous.
2.amp: And enter [bo] not into judgment [mishpat] with Your servant [ebed]: for in Your sight [panim] shall no man living [chay] be justified [tsadaq -- be declared righteous].
2.notes: The verse Paul builds justification by faith upon: lo yitsdaq le-phanekha kol-chay (H6663) -- before Your face no living being stands acquitted (cf. Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16; Psalm 130:3). David does not plead innocence; he pleads that the trial not be convened. The ebed asks for the Master's mercy precisely because he knows the Judge's verdict.

3.text: For the enemy has hunted my soul; he has crushed my life down to the ground; he has made me sit in dark places like those long dead.
3.amp: For the enemy [oyeb] has persecuted [radaph -- pursued] my soul [nephesh]; he has smitten [daka -- crushed] my life [chay] down to the ground [eretz]; he has made me to dwell [yashab] in darkness [machshak], as those that have been long [olam] dead [muth].
3.notes: The external trouble arrives only after the internal account is settled. radaph (H7291) and daka (H1792) -- pursued, then crushed flat -- and the machshakim (H4285), the dark places, where he sits like mete olam, the long dead. Lamentations 3:6 uses the identical phrase: a living man already in the tomb's shadow.

4.text: So my spirit faints and fails within me; my heart inside me is appalled and desolate.
4.amp: Therefore is my spirit [ruach] overwhelmed [ataph -- faints, wraps itself in weakness] within me; my heart [leb] within [tavek] me is desolate [shamem -- appalled, laid waste].
4.notes: ataph (H5848) is the fainting-wrap of Psalm 77:3 -- the ruach folding in on itself. shamem (H8074) is the desolation-word of ruined cities: the leb as a sacked town. David reports the collapse without embarrassment; the psalms never require composure as the price of prayer.

5.text: I call to mind the days long past; I ponder all that You have done; I muse over the work of Your hands.
5.amp: I remember [zakar] the days [yom] of old [qedem]; I meditate [hagah -- murmur, mutter over] on all Your works [poal]; I muse [siach -- go over aloud] on the work [maaseh] of Your hands [yad].
5.notes: The desolate heart's first discipline: zakar, hagah, siach (H2142, H1897, H7878) -- three verbs of deliberate remembering, aimed at qedem (H6924), the days of old, and at God's poal and maaseh. Asaph did the same in his night of doubt (cf. Psalm 77:11-12): when the present is dark, read God's record.

6.text: I stretch my hands out toward You; my soul is thirsty for You like drought-cracked ground. Selah.
6.amp: I stretch forth [paras -- spread out] my hands [yad] unto You: my soul [nephesh] thirsts after You, as a thirsty [ayeph -- weary, parched] land [eretz]. Selah.
6.notes: paras yadayim (H6566): palms spread open toward heaven, the posture of a beggar and of cracked ground opening for rain. eretz ayephah (H5889), the weary land of Psalm 63:1 -- David's soul as drought-country that cannot manufacture its own water. Thirst is the one qualification he brings.

7.text: Answer me quickly, O LORD -- my spirit is spent. Do not hide Your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the pit.
7.amp: Hear [anah -- answer] me speedily [maher], O LORD [YHWH]: my spirit [ruach] fails [kalah -- is consumed]: hide [satar] not Your face [panim] from me, lest I be like ['for I am become like', the KJV margin] unto them that go down [yarad] into the pit [bor].
7.notes: maher (H4118), quickly: the prayer of a man whose ruach kalah (H3615), whose spirit is burning down to the wick. The hidden panim (H5641, H6440) is the one loss that would finish him -- yorde bor (H3381, H953), the pit-descenders of Psalm 28:1 -- so the plea is for the face before the rescue.

8.text: Let me hear Your covenant love in the morning, for in You I trust; make me know the way I should walk, for to You I lift up my soul.
8.amp: Cause me to hear [shama] Your lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love] in the morning [boqer]; for in You do I trust [batach]: cause me to know [yada] the way [derek] wherein I should walk [yalak]; for I lift up [nasa] my soul [nephesh] unto You.
8.notes: The psalm's most-prayed verse: chesed (H2617) requested as the first sound of boqer (H1242) -- morning mercies, before the day's news. Two petitions on two warrants: hear love, because batach; know the derek, because nasa nephesh (H5375, H5315) -- the lifted soul of Psalm 25:1. Trust and surrender as the two credentials.

9.text: Rescue me from my enemies, O LORD; I have fled to You to be hidden.
9.amp: Deliver [natsal -- snatch away] me, O LORD [YHWH], from mine enemies [oyeb]: I flee unto You to hide me ['hide me with thee', kasah, the KJV margin].
9.notes: The margin preserves the Hebrew's intimacy: elekha kissiti -- 'with You I have covered myself' -- kasah (H3680), the covering-verb of forgiveness in Psalm 32:1, here the covering of refuge. He hides in God the way the pardoned man's sin is hidden by God.

10.text: Train me to carry out Your will, for You are my God; may Your good Spirit guide me onto level ground.
10.amp: Teach [lamad] me to do [asah] Your will [ratson]; for You are my God [Elohim]: Your spirit [ruach] is good [tov]; lead [nachah] me into the land [eretz] of uprightness [mishor -- level ground, equity].
10.notes: Not 'teach me Your will' but 'teach me to DO it' -- lamad la-asot ratson (H3925, H6213, H7522): the request is for obedience, not information. ruchakha tovah -- Your good Spirit -- one of the Old Testament's clearest namings of the Spirit as guide (cf. Nehemiah 9:20), and nachah (H5148), the shepherd-verb, onto eretz mishor (H4334), level ground where a crushed man can walk without falling again.

11.text: For the sake of Your name, O LORD, give me life; in Your righteousness bring my soul out of trouble.
11.amp: Quicken [chayah -- revive] me, O LORD [YHWH], for Your name's [shem] sake: for Your righteousness' [tsedaqah] sake bring [yatsa] my soul [nephesh] out of trouble [tsarah].
11.notes: Two le-maan clauses -- for the sake of Your shem, for the sake of Your tsedaqah -- and nothing for David's sake at all; the man who could not stand in judgment (v. 2) asks to be revived on God's account only. chayah (H2421), Psalm 119's heartbeat-request, and yatsa (H3318) out of the tsarah: life and exit, both in God's name.

12.text: And in Your covenant love, silence my enemies and destroy all who press upon my soul -- for I am Your servant.
12.amp: And of Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love] cut off [tsamath -- silence, exterminate] mine enemies [oyeb], and destroy [abad] all them that afflict [tsarar -- press, distress] my soul [nephesh]: for I am Your servant [ebed].
12.notes: The imprecation arrives last and is grounded in chesed -- covenant love toward the servant necessarily means judgment on those crushing him (v. 3). The psalm's closing words are its whole argument in three: ki ani avdekha (H5650), for I am Your servant. Not righteous (v. 2), not strong (v. 4), not deserving (v. 11) -- Yours. That is the penitent's entire case, and it is sufficient.
